newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says Europe car sales on track '97.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says Europe car sales on track '97.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Wednesday that its sales in Europe are on track to meet its forecast of 230,000 cars sold in 1997.
"We give no forecasts for sales but sales in the first quarter in Europe were in line with the target to sell 230,000 cars this year," Volvo Cars managing director Tuve Johannesson told a seminar.
He said that it will be a long time before Volvo Cars starts new production in the U.S.
"Such an investment must be made in partnership with a new car model but there is no such decision at the moment," Johannesson said.
Volvo Cars is currently investing in the Asian region and the company has set itself a target to sell 100,000 cars a year in that region.
"We see Southeast Asia as a growth market and we are investing hard to set ourselves up there," he said.
"We have a goal to sell 100,000 cars."
